correctness.rationale: The verifier reconstructs all \(64\) binary length-six words and their distinct one-deletion descendant sets, builds the complete compatibility graph, and exhaustively enumerates all maximal cliques with exact integer bitsets. It obtains \(62,707\) maximal cliques, maximum size \(10\), and exactly nine size-ten cliques. It then checks pairwise descendant disjointness for every maximum, recomputes their common four-word intersection, descendant-union sizes \(26,28,28,28,30,30,30,30,32\), identifies the unique 32-word descendant partition as \(\mathrm{VT}_0(6)\), and exhausts the four reversal/complement transformations to obtain orbit sizes \(2,2,2,1,1,1\). A separate NetworkX maximal-clique implementation matched the same maximal-clique count and nine maxima.

originality.rationale: The scalar optimum \(A(6,1)=10\) and the existence of at least one nonperfect optimum are prior. The accepted contribution is the complete nine-code census, universal four-word core, unique-perfect statement with exact nonperfect coverage histogram, and six-orbit decomposition under reversal and complement. The closest inspected sources do not imply these classification statements, and targeted published-finding corpus and web searches over exact parameters, replacement words, aliases, coverage, and equivalence formulations found no matching census.
residual_risks: An obscure, unindexed, or unpublished finite enumeration may contain the same nine-code census.
The symmetry statement is intentionally restricted to reversal and global bit complement; no full-automorphism classification is asserted.

value.rationale: Length six is the first small case singled out in the foundational survey where an optimal VT code admits an explicit same-size replacement producing a nonperfect optimum. Completing that observation into an exact all-maxima classification answers a natural structural question: it shows there are only nine optimizers, that perfectness is unique, that all nine share a nontrivial four-word core, and that the nonperfect optimizers fall into precise coverage and symmetry types. This is a canonical finite extremal classification rather than an arbitrary slice or a recomputation of the known scalar optimum.
